sources: Hyland, K. (1998). Hedging in scientific research articles. John Benjamins. https://doi.org/10.1075/pbns.54
Hyland, K. (2005). Stance and engagement: A model of interaction in academic discourse. Discourse Studies, 7(2), 173-192. https://doi.org/10.1177/1461445605050365
Hyland, K. (2001). Humble servants of the discipline? Self-mention in research articles. English for Specific Purposes, 20(3), 207-226. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0889-4906(00)00012-0
matching: Case-insensitive whole-word match on [a-z]+ tokens of body paragraphs (abstract, sections, appendices), after author-year citations, figure, table, equation and section references are removed as in tools/roadmap/g26_translation.py; captions, front-matter elements and back matter are counted separately. Rates are per 1,000 tokens. Every item is counted as written; no disambiguation. 'polysemous' lists the items that also carry a non-stance sense in Earth-science prose; rates are reported with and without them, and their precision is to be measured on a hand-checked sample before any rate is interpreted.
